assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: Five separate @TableTest methods: addsItemsFromTheCatalogue, removesItemsFromTheCart, appliesCouponsToTheCart, checksOutTheCart, calculatesTheCartTotal

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Add has 6 rows (new, stack, unknown, zero, negative); Remove has 4 rows; Apply has 7 rows; Checkout has 7 rows; Total has 10 rows. Each focuses on its operation.

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: addsItemsFromTheCatalogue, removesItemsFromTheCart, appliesCouponsToTheCart, calculatesTheCartTotal, checksOutTheCart are five distinct methods

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions (e.g. 'Cart with items' as an input column, not implied from a previous row).
assertions.evidence: Each row in all tables has explicit input columns (Cart Before, Catalogue, Stock, etc.) and does not reference prior rows. Each is self-contained.

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart table has 'Active Coupon Before' and 'Active Coupon After?' columns showing state transitions

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart tests validity/replacement only (expired, unknown, replace scenarios). calculatesTheCartTotal tests price effects (PERCENT 20, FIXED 5.00, PRODUCT Widget 5.00)

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Active Coupon After?, Success?, Message?, Success?, Message Mentions?, Total?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'Add new item to empty cart', 'Expired coupon does not replace the active coupon', 'Insufficient stock by one unit' describe conditions, not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Column header 'Product Id' appears in addsItemsFromTheCatalogue and removesItemsFromTheCart tables; should be 'Product' per reference decomposition

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 5 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Catalogue column shows prices [Widget: 10.00]; Coupon In Store shows definitions (PERCENT 10, FIXED 5.00, PRODUCT Widget 3.00, EXPIRED); Active Coupon column shows coupon types

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects (e.g. Map → Cart, Map → InventoryService, map → Coupon). Test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter methods: parseCatalogue, parseCart, parseInventory, parseCoupon. Method bodies call CartService methods directly without constructing objects from raw values

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter — not spread across separate sparse columns for coupon type, value, and target product.
assertions.evidence: The coupon column uses raw enum form (e.g., 'PERCENT 10', 'FIXED 5.00', 'PRODUCT Widget 3.00') parsed by a custom @TypeConverter, but the reference spec requires 'readable shorthand (e.g. 20% cart, $5 off) or map syntax [type: PERCENT, value: 10]'. The implementation uses space-delimited enum strings instead.

assertions.text: Columns representing maps use standard TableTest map syntax — [k: v, k2: v2] for entries and [:] for empty map — not a custom bracket notation.
assertions.evidence: Cart, Catalogue, and Inventory columns all use standard syntax: '[Widget: 2]', '[Widget: 9.99, Gadget: 4.50]', '[:]' for empty, with @TypeConverter methods that parse these into domain objects.

assertions.text: @Description annotations do not merely repeat information that the scenario names already convey.
assertions.evidence: The 'addsItemsFromTheCatalogue' @Description states 'Adding a product already in the cart increases its quantity rather than replacing it (assumption — the rules don't state this explicitly)' and 'Quantity must be a positive integer', which are deliberate assumptions not evident from scenario names alone.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: The 'addsItemsFromTheCatalogue' table has varying expectations: '[Widget: 2]' vs '[Widget: 3]' vs '[:]', and success values of true/false. The 'calculatesTheCartTotal' table shows different totals (30.00, 40.00, 16.00, 15.00, 0.00) depending on coupon type and cart contents, falsifiable by implementation.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Column headers ('Cart Before', 'Product Id', 'Quantity', 'Cart After?', 'Success?', 'Message?') and scenario names ('Add new item to empty cart', 'Product not in the catalogue') make the rules clear without reading the method body.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or method name) states what the code under test does, not an external fact it depends on.
assertions.evidence: Method names 'addsItemsFromTheCatalogue', 'removesItemsFromTheCart', 'appliesCouponsToTheCart', 'checksOutTheCart', 'calculatesTheCartTotal' all describe actions the CartService performs, not external facts.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: The 'calculatesTheCartTotal' table uses a value set '{PERCENT 50, FIXED 5.00}' in the 'Empty cart, any coupon' row to cover 'any coupon' quantification. The 'appliesCouponsToTheCart' table covers all three coupon types (PERCENT, FIXED, PRODUCT) across separate rows.

assertions.text: A comparison criterion applied by the assertion must be stated on the published surface.
assertions.evidence: The 'checksOutTheCart' method asserts containment via 'Message Mentions?' column header and @Description stating 'must contain', and 'calculatesTheCartTotal' uses BigDecimal.compareTo with @Description explaining 'floored at zero'.

assertions.text: Across @TableTest methods in one class, the same observable quantity carries the same column name.
assertions.evidence: The 'addsItemsFromTheCatalogue' table uses 'Product Id' while 'removesItemsFromTheCart' uses 'Product Id', but 'appliesCouponsToTheCart' uses 'Coupon Code' and 'Coupon In Store' for coupon-related inputs. More critically, 'Cart Before' vs 'Cart Items' appear in different tables for the same input quantity (remove uses 'Cart Before', checkout uses 'Cart Items').
